title: Nearly 3 Million Eels Gather at an Underwater Mountain—But What For? - Nautilus
gist: Researchers publishing in Royal Society Open Science counted roughly 2.8 million basketwork eels at Patience Seamount off Tasmania in May 2023, with lower counts in March 2024 and April 2025 attributed to seasonality rather than population decline.

insights.claim: Researchers estimated about 2.8 million basketwork eels gathered at Patience Seamount, an underwater mountain off Tasmania, in May 2023, the first count of this annual aggregation.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Baseline biodiversity data on seamounts matters for deep-sea fishing and mining regulation debates.
insights.quote: around 2.8 million eels populating the region in May 2023

insights.claim: Significantly lower eel numbers in March 2024 and April 2025 were attributed by the team to seasonal changes rather than population decline, with numbers peaking in May.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Survey timing can create false decline signals; relevant to environmental impact assessments.
insights.quote: which the team chalks up to seasonal changes rather than a declining eel population

insights.claim: The purpose of the annual eel congregation remains an open question in the reporting.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Unknown ecological function argues for precaution in seamount resource exploitation.
